summary: Learn shock-responsive design, targeting, payments, and reporting in 5 days. Build practical recovery tools for real operations.
lede: Social protection systems in disaster recovery help professionals coordinate benefits, targeting, payments, referrals, and monitoring so households can recover faster and institutions can demonstrate results. This course develops practical capability in shock-responsive targeting, payment delivery, referral coordination, grievance handling, and results reporting. You will work with vulnerability analysis, shock-trigger mapping, beneficiary registry review, payment channel assessment, recovery action plans, and results frameworks. The course also introduces social registry interoperability, anticipatory action linkages, digital case-management workflows, and practical tools such as trigger tables, beneficiary flow maps, and reporting templates.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who manage or support social protection systems in disaster recovery settings and need practical tools for targeting, coordination, and reporting.
prerequisites: Participants should have a working understanding of disaster recovery, social protection, or humanitarian program operations. Familiarity with program coordination, basic monitoring and evaluation, and beneficiary targeting concepts will help you move faster through the applied exercises. Programming or coding is not required. You should bring a laptop for spreadsheet-based exercises and template work, and be prepared to review sample registry data, trigger tables, and recovery planning tools. Advanced concepts such as digital registry interoperability and anticipatory action are taught at operational awareness level, not engineering depth.
